newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's CPP rate falls in December vs November.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's CPP rate falls in December vs November.

text.p: Mexico's CPP fell 1.06 basis points in December from the month before to 26.97 percent, the Banco de Mexico said.
The CPP, the average bank cost of borrowing from the public, was at 28.03 percent in November.
The central bank said the CCP, the average bank term desposit cost measured in pesos in Mexican banks, was 28.19 percent for December.
The CCP eventually will become a substitute for the CPP, with the aim of better reflecting the cost of those term deposits for the banks, the central bank said.

The Banco de Mexico also said the CCP-UDIs, the CPP measured in UDIs, an inflation indexed investment unit, was at 7.27 percent for the month, down from 7.71 percent in November. Banco de Mexico publishes the various rates to give a better idea to the public of the cost of borrowing.
